hook: When prices fall, one boring habit quietly lowers the average price you pay for investments.

blocks.narration: When prices fall, one boring habit quietly lowers the average price you pay for investments. It is called dollar cost averaging.
blocks.visual: A clay shopping cart rolls into a market stall where price tags are dropping, warm light

blocks.narration: The idea is simple. You invest the same amount on a set schedule, like one hundred dollars every month, no matter what.
blocks.visual: A clay hand drops a coin into a slot on the first day of each month as calendar pages turn

blocks.narration: In month one, each share costs ten dollars, so your hundred dollars buys exactly ten shares. Nothing exciting so far.
blocks.visual: Ten small clay shares drop into a basket under a price tag showing a ten

blocks.narration: In month two, the market drops and shares cost five dollars. The same hundred dollars now buys twenty shares instead.
blocks.visual: The price tag flips to a five and twenty shares tumble into the basket

blocks.narration: Month three, prices recover to ten dollars, and you buy ten more shares. You spent three hundred dollars for forty shares.
blocks.visual: The price tag flips back to ten, ten more shares drop, the basket now nicely full

blocks.narration: That works out to seven dollars fifty per share, even though the average price over those months was about eight thirty-three.
blocks.visual: Two clay scales compare side by side, the cost-per-share side resting lower

blocks.narration: You automatically bought more when things were on sale. It also removes the stress of trying to pick the perfect day.
blocks.visual: A relaxed clay figure sips coffee while an automatic machine keeps dropping coins on schedule

blocks.narration: It does not guarantee a profit, but it builds a steady habit. Follow for more money math that actually makes sense.
blocks.visual: The basket of shares glows softly as the camera slowly pulls back

captions.hook_line: How falling prices can actually lower what you pay 🧮
captions.body: Investing a fixed amount on a schedule buys more shares when prices are low and fewer when they are high. In the example, $300 buys 40 shares at an average cost of $7.50 while the average price was $8.33.
